newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt markets finish flat after dreary day.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt markets finish flat after dreary day.

text.p: * NZ debt markets finish flat after quiet day
* US to dictate developments in short term
New Zealand yields closed largely unchanged after a dreary Monday session, and dealers said there was little economic news on the domestic horizon to move the market.
"There were a few flows on Friday but they more or less cancelled each other out, and the political polls over the weekend pretty much cancelled each other out as well," a Wellington dealer said.
"So yes, we sit here. More and more people are just sitting on the sidelines waiting for the election."
New Zealand is due for a general election on October 12.

Long bonds remained around three pips weaker throughout the day after opening slightly lower on the back of a small sell-off in the United States. The 10-years finished at 8.04 percent, while the three-year maturities ended off two.
Ninety day bank bills hovered around 9.95 percent on thin volume.
Dealers said the U.S. market would dictate the direction of the longer New Zealand bonds in the short term.
"I think the U.S. is probably going to try to rally a wee bit further, and we might have a look at 8.00 percent or a bit under in the long bonds," one dealer said.
NZD VS 3 YR 10 YR * NZD 3-YR/10-YR SPREAD

New Zealand three-year bonds slightly underperformed other dollar bloc countries on Monday, with the spread against the U.S. widening five points to 192. Dealers said that after the sharp escalation in spreads seen in recent weeks, New Zealand's current position at the lower end of the range had caught a few people by surprise.
One said the NZ/US 10-year spread could easily get back to 150-160 points over the week.

"It's difficult to see it go a lot lower, but the market is so flow driven and people are so keen to do nothing that I guess we could see it squeeze in further. Twenty points either way wouldn't surprise me -- it's that thin," one said.
